title: Pork and Ginger Gyoza
subtitle: Japanese pan-fried pork dumplings
excerpt: Homemade gyoza filled with pork, ginger, and salted cabbage, pan-fried until the base is crisp then steamed to cook the filling through. They take time to fold but the method is straightforward and the results are much better than shop-bought.
sourceNotes: Based on the Japanese gyoza tradition, itself derived from the Chinese jiaozi. The pan-fry and steam method produces the characteristic crisp bottom with a tender top.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncooked on a tray until solid, then transfer to a bag. Cook from frozen, adding 3 minutes to the steaming time.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch and freeze half.

content.text: Salt the shredded cabbage and leave it for 10 minutes, then squeeze out all the water before adding to the filling. This is the most important step; wet cabbage will make the filling loose and the wrappers may burst during cooking.

items.prepNote: very finely shredded, salted for 10 minutes then squeezed dry
kept covered with a damp cloth while you work

content.text: Toss the shredded cabbage with a good pinch of salt and set aside for 10 minutes. Squeeze firmly in your hands until very dry.
Mix the pork mince, dried cabbage, ginger, garlic, spring onion, soy sauce, and sesame oil in a bowl until combined.

Place a gyoza wrapper on a clean surface. Spoon about 1 teaspoon of filling into the centre. Wet the edge of the wrapper with a little water, fold in half over the filling, and pleat and press the edges to seal. Sit each gyoza upright as you go.
Heat the sunflower oil in a large non-stick frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the gyoza flat-side down in a single layer. Fry for 2 to 3 minutes until the bases are deep golden.
Pour 60ml of water into the pan and cover with a lid. Steam for 4 to 5 minutes. The water should fully evaporate. The filling should be cooked through.
Remove the lid and cook for 1 minute more to re-crisp the bases. Serve immediately with soy sauce for dipping.

items.cause: Filling too wet or wrapper not sealed firmly
items.fix: Squeeze cabbage drier and press edges firmly with damp fingers.
Keep the lid on until all water is gone, then fry 1 minute more.
